blocks.text: The two witnesses are described with a deliberately layered set of images. Their power over rain, water turned to blood, and plagues recalls figures associated with Elijah and Moses, while the olive trees and lampstands of verse 4 draw on Zechariah’s imagery. These connections do not settle the witnesses’ precise identity; rather, they show that the chapter portrays their testimony through familiar scriptural patterns.

Revelation repeatedly reworks imagery from Israel’s Scriptures, including Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Exodus, Zechariah, Genesis, and Psalms. Its seals, trumpets, and bowls also form major sevenfold judgment sequences, with interludes and recurring motifs. This wider pattern helps frame the seventh trumpet in Revelation 11 as part of an extended, carefully patterned vision rather than as an isolated scene.
